original_question: Determine whether there exists an icc non inner amenable group G such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is not elementarily equivalent to L(F2).
target_in_paper: Problem 16 in the section "McDuff and Property Gamma factors": Does there exist an icc non inner amenable group G such that L(G) is not elementarily equivalent to L(F_2)?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official target almost verbatim: it asks for an existence statement about an icc, non-inner-amenable group G and compares its group von Neumann algebra specifically with L(F_2) via elementary equivalence. It also correctly stays with the narrower group-factor question rather than broadening to the nearby problem about arbitrary non-Gamma II_1 factors.
missing_details: Identify the exact in-paper source as Problem 16 in the section "McDuff and Property Gamma factors."
State that F_2 is the free group on two generators.
Make explicit that L(G) denotes the group von Neumann algebra of the discrete group G.

Spell out the paper's notion of elementary equivalence: II_1 factors M and N are elementarily equivalent if there exist ultrafilters U and V such that the tracial ultrapowers M^U and N^V are isomorphic.
If full stand-alone readability is desired, unpack icc as meaning that every nontrivial conjugacy class of G is infinite.
refined_question: Does there exist a discrete group G that is icc (that is, every nontrivial conjugacy class is infinite) and not inner amenable such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is not elementarily equivalent to the free group factor L(F_2), where F_2 is the free group on two generators and where two II_1 factors M and N are called elementarily equivalent if there exist ultrafilters U and V for which the tracial ultrapowers M^U and N^V are isomorphic?
justification: The paper's standing notation defines what it means for II_1 factors to be elementarily equivalent, and the exact official formulation matching your draft is Problem 16 in the section "McDuff and Property Gamma factors." The immediately preceding Problem 15 is the broader neighboring question about non-Gamma factors in general, so the paper-faithful refinement should keep the icc and non-inner-amenable group hypotheses and the specific comparison with L(F_2).
